meta.title: Fatoora Hub | ZATCA Phase 2 Compliance as an API
meta.description: A headless compliance gateway for Saudi e-invoicing. Keep your POS, ERP, or store exactly as it is — send ordinary invoice JSON and get back a signed, ZATCA-compliant invoice with a TLV QR code and a PDF/A-3 document.

hero.titleSuffix: Keep your software. Keep your database.
hero.description: FatooraHub sits between your product and the Saudi tax authority. You send ordinary invoice JSON — line items, quantities, VAT rates, a customer — and get back a signed, compliant invoice with a TLV QR code and a ready-to-send PDF/A-3. Nothing about your POS, ERP, or checkout changes.
highlights: A pure business-domain REST API — your developers never touch UBL XML, ASN.1 OIDs, or ECDSA signing
ICV and invoice-hash chains serialized per device, so two concurrent checkouts can never corrupt the chain
ZATCA Schematron validation runs locally, before anything reaches your compliance profile
HTTP 208 and 409 duplicate recovery handled natively, so a network retry never double-bills

features.eyebrow: What we take off your team
features.title: Eight burdens you stop carrying
features.subtitle: Each of these is a real engineering project on its own. None of them are your product, and all of them are permanent.

items.title: A pure business-domain REST API
items.burden: Reading UBL 2.1 XML, namespace prefixes, ASN.1 OIDs, and certificate formats, then re-modelling all of it in your own domain language.
items.relief: Your developers write line items, quantities, unit prices, VAT rates, and a customer. We map, validate, sign, and package the UBL, the QR, and the PDF/A-3.

items.title: Concurrency: ICV and the invoice-hash chain
items.burden: Every device must emit a strictly sequential ICV and cryptographically embed the previous invoice's hash. Two checkouts reading the same value in the same instant permanently invalidates that device's chain.
items.relief: Sequence assignment is serialized per device at the database layer. Concurrent traffic queues instead of colliding — no gaps, no duplicates, no broken chains.

items.title: Pre-validation before ZATCA sees anything
items.burden: Every malformed invoice you send is recorded against the taxpayer's compliance profile on government servers. Repetition invites formal inquiries.
items.relief: Official Schematron rules and national business rules run locally on every request, so a broken invoice fails against us instead of against your standing.

items.title: Rejection and warning governance
items.burden: ZATCA requires a new ICV after a rejection, but the next invoice's PIH must still link to the rejected document's hash. Roll back the counter or reuse the previous hash and the whole chain dies.
items.relief: Rejected states are tracked deterministically and the chain advances through them automatically. Non-blocking warnings are surfaced separately from hard rejections, so you decide whether they matter.

items.title: Duplicate recovery: HTTP 208 and 409
items.burden: ZATCA deduplicates by hash for 24 hours. A retried standard invoice comes back as 208 Already Reported; a retried simplified invoice comes back as 409 — which the rules say must be treated as success.
items.relief: Both are handled natively. The cleared artifacts are extracted, the invoice is marked reported, and the retry recovers idempotently instead of double-billing or tripping anti-abuse.

items.title: Offline and latency resilience at the till
items.burden: Government endpoints spike and go down. If every checkout waits on a round trip to Riyadh, the queue at the register stops moving.
items.relief: Simplified invoices are signed and QR-coded on our side, then reported inside the legal 24-hour window by a background worker that retries through transient outages.

items.title: Device onboarding and certificates
items.burden: A device cannot go to production on trust. It needs a CSR, a portal OTP, and a compliance check — repeated for every branch and every register, by hand.
items.relief: Register a device with its portal OTP from the dashboard and watch its phase, ICV, and certificate expiry in one place. Renew before the certificate lapses.

items.title: Long-term regulatory maintenance
items.burden: Schematron rules, tax reason codes, and enforcement waves keep moving. An in-house integration is never finished, and every change pulls an engineer off the roadmap.
items.relief: We are a dedicated compliance layer. When ZATCA publishes a change we ship it centrally. Your application code does not change.

developers.title: Business JSON in. Signed, compliant invoice out.
developers.subtitle: Two endpoints cover almost all traffic. Everything else — the full signed XML, a PDF/A-3, retries, devices, API keys — is a REST call away.

items.title: No XML, no cryptography, no certificates in your codebase
items.description: If your team can POST JSON, they can invoice. UBL 2.1, the TLV QR, and the ECDSA signature are our problem, not a dependency of yours.

items.title: Typed contracts and real error bodies
items.description: Every endpoint has a documented request and response schema. Failures come back as RFC 7807 problem details with a field-level error list, not a stack trace.

items.title: Pagination and filtering built in
items.description: Numbered pages, plus filters on status, invoice type, date range, free-text search, device, and taxpayer.

items.title: Idempotent recovery built in
items.description: A single failed invoice can be retried on its own, or every failed invoice on a page can be re-queued in one call.

items.title: The signed document is yours to keep
items.description: Pull the base64 signed UBL and the TLV QR as data, or stream a PDF/A-3 with the XML embedded — no secondary document engine required.

faq.title: Straight answers to the hard ones
faq.subtitle: Including the one about whether your engineers could just build this themselves.

items.question: Can our developers just build this with AI and the official SDK?
items.answer: They can write the signing code — the SDK makes that part genuinely easy. But the SDK is stateless: it doesn't run your servers, hold your transaction locks, or retry a failed submission overnight. Concurrency, chain continuity, duplicate recovery, and device onboarding are weeks of operational engineering followed by permanent maintenance. That layer is what you're buying.

items.question: Why not just use Daftra or Wafeq?
items.answer: If you want to retire your current POS or billing software and run everything inside one ERP, those are good products and they'll do the job. But they're a replacement, not an integration. FatooraHub is the opposite trade: you keep your software, your database, and your checkout flow exactly as they are, and we handle the compliance layer behind a single API.

items.question: What happens if ZATCA is down or slow?
items.answer: Your register keeps moving. We sign the invoice and produce the compliant QR on our side, so the receipt prints immediately, and a background worker reports it inside the legal 24-hour window with automatic retries through transient outages. A government-side outage never reaches your checkout line.

items.question: How do you handle invalid invoices or rejections?
items.answer: Schema and business rules run locally before we transmit anything, so a malformed invoice fails against us instead of landing on your compliance profile. When ZATCA does reject one, the chain still advances correctly: the next invoice gets a new ICV and its PIH links to the rejected document's hash, exactly as the rules require. Your device stays valid.

items.question: Do I need to change my current POS or accounting software?
items.answer: No. FatooraHub is a headless gateway, not an application. Your team keeps the software it already knows, and your business data stays in your own database — we act strictly as the bridge to ZATCA.

items.question: What happens if I exceed my monthly invoice limit?
items.answer: Upgrade to a higher plan at any time, or buy additional invoice bundles at fair prices. There is no interruption to your invoicing while that happens.

realityCheck.title: Yes, your engineers can write the SDK calls. No, that isn't the hard part.
realityCheck.subtitle: The official ZATCA SDK is a set of cryptographic primitives, and it is stateless. It doesn't run your servers, commit your database transactions, or operate the queue that retries a failed submission at 3am. Writing the integration is the easy 10%.
realityCheck.sdkTitle: What the SDK (and AI) hand you
hubItems: High-concurrency ICV and hash-chain serialization under database row locks
Local Schematron pre-validation before ZATCA ever sees the invoice
Rejection governance that preserves chain continuity across HTTP 400s
Native HTTP 208 clearance and HTTP 409 reporting recovery
Buffered submission inside the 24-hour B2C reporting window
Device registration and certificate lifecycle from one dashboard
Regulatory changes handled centrally when ZATCA updates the rules
A business-domain REST API your team can read in an afternoon
realityCheck.footer: You can prompt a model to write the signing code. You cannot prompt it to run your production infrastructure at 3am.

comparison.title: Both paths produce a compliant invoice
comparison.subtitle: The difference is who owns the other 90%, and what your engineers are doing instead of building your product.

rows.inhouse: Your team designs, builds, versions, and documents every endpoint.
rows.hub: A documented REST API you send ordinary business JSON to.

rows.inhouse: Architect and load-test row locking per register yourself.
rows.hub: Per-device serialization at the database layer, already proven.

rows.inhouse: Discover the 208 / 409 / 400 quirks in production, one incident at a time.
rows.hub: Duplicate recovery and rejection-state tracking built in.

rows.inhouse: Synchronous calls to ZATCA stall the register during a government-side spike.
rows.hub: Signing happens on our side; reporting retries in the background.

rows.inhouse: Run the CSR, OTP, and sample-invoice steps by hand, per branch.
rows.hub: Register from the dashboard with a portal OTP; track phase and expiry.

rows.inhouse: An engineer is pulled off the roadmap to patch validation rules.
rows.hub: Shipped centrally by us. Your code is untouched.

rows.inhouse: Most PDF engines can't produce PDF/A-3 with embedded signed XML.
rows.hub: Generated natively, with the signed XML embedded in the file.

comparison.footnote: Switching to Daftra, Wafeq, or Odoo is a different decision altogether — those are full ERP suites. You'd be replacing your POS, migrating your databases, and retraining your cashiers. FatooraHub assumes you're keeping all of it.

security.title: Your certificates can't move money
security.subtitle: A ZATCA certificate is a document stamp, not a financial credential. It's worth being precise about what we hold on your behalf and why.

items.title: No financial authority
items.description: A ZATCA CSID proves a document's origin and integrity. It cannot initiate a payment, move funds, or reach a bank account.

items.title: Portal OTPs are never stored
items.description: The one-time code from the ZATCA portal is held in memory for the duration of the onboarding handshake and is never written to disk.

items.title: Tenant isolation is structural
items.description: Every client's data and keys are separated by query filters applied at the data layer, so a cross-tenant read isn't a bug anyone has to remember to prevent.
